title: Eagle-eye box file
description: A morphological box: decisions (dims), their options, and the edges between options. Documentation of the shape; render.mjs validates it with hand-rolled checks so nothing needs installing.

eyebrow.description: Small caps line above the title. Sheet number, date, revision.

problem.description: The brief: what this whole box decides, in plain words, for a reader who does not know the domain. A fact about the decision, not about any row — render.mjs warns about a row that has no dims[].problem, and refuses a box that has no problem. Two to five sentences, STE rules. It refuses a problem that is absent, not a string, or only whitespace; minLength and the pattern above say the same thing.

who.description: Who the decision affects. Optional, and one plain sentence — there is no people model. render.mjs refuses a blank one; leave the field out instead.

when.description: When the decision must be settled. Optional, and one plain sentence — the renderer reads no date, so "not known" is a valid value. render.mjs refuses a blank one; leave the field out instead.

question.description: The decision as a question. Shown when the row is opened, under the row name.

problem.description: What this row decides, in plain words, for a reader outside the domain: the terms it rests on, why the choice exists, what turns on it. Two to five sentences, STE rules. Opens the 'In short' block above the cards. The renderer warns when a row has none — no derivation can supply it, and a row name like 'Reachable by whom' explains itself to nobody.

id.description: Unique across the whole box. Convention: <dim>-<word>. The id is machine state. It appears in the box file and in the restore code, and never in chat.

short.description: Sheet-cell wording. Two or three words. Required, because this is the name Claude says in chat. Without it the only handle is the id, and an id names nothing to a reader. See SKILL.md, 'Names in chat'.

chosen.description: Exactly one per row. The current position.

strawman.description: This option answers one of the four coverage questions: none / opposite / later / by hand. The flag records coverage, not provenance — set it even when somebody proposed the option, and keep the src that says who did. A row whose 'none' answer came from the ticket is still covered.

src.description: Where this option was proposed: ticket, document, chat turn.

rel.description: Keyed by option id. Every option should have an entry.

why.description: What this option is and why it was on the table. One to three sentences, STE.

rel.description: Edges from this option. Tuple: [targetOptionId, kind, why, tier?, src?]. Target must be in another row.

prefixItems.description: conf: rules the target out. req: requires the target.
src — required for measured and sourced

notes.description: Things that are not edges: preferences, caveats, history.

suspected.description: Edges that failed the audit. Listed on the page, colour nothing.

presets.description: Guided walkthroughs shown as chips. REQUIRED, at least two, and at least one must carry a step with `set` so the reader meets a configuration that is not the baseline. render.mjs enforces both. See SKILL.md, 'Presets', for the archetypes.

predict.description: With set: start a coach prediction for that change.

open.description: dim id to open in Findings, or null to close.
